body.title: Before you connect a private repository
body.intro: Read this once before pointing the harness at a real repo. Everything below is enforced in code by the deployment you are running — this checklist tells you where.

items.statement: Agent commands run in an ephemeral Docker container, one per task, destroyed on completion or timeout. Allowed commands are read-only inspection, test runners, linters, builds, and lockfile-based installs.
items.enforcedBy: Section 5 command allow-list (enforced in code, not docs)

items.statement: Destructive deletes, force-push, secret-file reads, package publishing, infrastructure-changing commands and arbitrary network pipelines are blocked, as is anything touching the plan's forbidden paths.
Network egress is restricted to pinned official package registries (npmjs.com, pypi.org) or a self-hosted mirror — no other destinations.
API keys are encrypted at rest and decrypted only inside the model routing layer — they never enter model context, prompts, or logs.
items.enforcedBy: Section 1 key vault + Section 3 decrypt boundary

items.statement: Agents never merge. The system contains no merge call at all: you approve the review in-app, then click merge yourself on GitHub.
items.enforcedBy: Section 2 merge guard + Section 8 review gate

items.statement: No agent command executes until a human approves the plan that names the files it will touch and the paths it must not touch.
Every approval, pause, takeover, key change, and blocked command is written to an append-only audit log you can inspect.
